Found a FOURTH hole beyond the three described: the interceptor was never installed on staging at all (config/initializers/mailer_interceptor.rb registered it 'unless Rails.env.production?'), so fixing delivering_email alone would have changed nothing.

Fixed in Flow 9 phase 1 (4a456c7). Dark --bg-nav drops to bg.sunken (26 27 29) so it no longer collides with --bg-page, AND .app-sidebar gains border-r border-border-default. Took the canvas's both-halves fix over the bead's option (a) border-only: §3.2 now records the rule that separation is by surface and border, never shadow. Light mode gains the border too, which is a small visible change there. Verified in the built CSS, not just the source.

Fixed in Flow 9 phase 1 (4a456c7). Part 1 was exactly as described: staff_nav had no quartermaster branch. Inventory nav membership now keys on inventory_access via one shared helper, matching the condition InventoryController already admits on.

Part 2 was OVERSTATED in this bead and in the canvas. The claim was that /inventory/email_rules highlights Inventory and leaves Emails inert. Neither half was true: Inventory's regex was %r{\A/inventory/categor}, which does not match email_rules, and Emails fell through to current_page? which DOES match its index exactly. Since inventory_email_rules has only index and create, there was no GET route where it failed. The bug was latent, not live. Fixed anyway as hardening: active state is now a deepest-matching path prefix resolved across the whole nav set, so no item depends on an exact match that happens to be sufficient.

Closing per Dan (2026-09-17): reopen if flakiness comes back.

The specific coin-flip found on the Flow 9 branch is gone. dashboards_spec.rb asserted include(member.full_name) against rendered HTML while signed in as that member; Faker draws apostrophe surnames like O'Conner, which the view escapes to O'Conner, so whether it passed came down to the random order seed. That is the same 'green on eight reruns, red once' signature as this bead, but the original Flow 4 sighting was never captured, so the link stays unproven.

Fixed by deleting the assertion rather than escaping around it: it could never fail anyway. The shell renders current_user.full_name in the profile menu on every authenticated page, so the spec passed on the chrome — proven by deleting the dashboard's whole subline and watching it still pass. The inventory spec had the same shape and was never flaky at all (that view uses <%== into a script tag, so the name is not escaped there); it now asserts against the parsed window.itemHistory payload and fails when the trail is empty.

Verified: whole suite 935/0 with every user forced to 'Ethan O'Conner', which is the condition that used to break it. CI green on all four jobs (run 35175559760).
